attempts.finding: Every completed case encountered non-object nested component payloads in the open-ended write_spec object schema. A separate exact-payload round-trip probe reproduced malformed nesting on both Gemini models; the same payload transported as a JSON string was preserved exactly.
attempts.resolution: The development adapter now accepts the complete spec as a JSON-encoded string and explicitly rejects invalid JSON or a non-object decoded value. The pricing engine, skill, approval checks and runtime fingerprint are unchanged.
limitations: Four in-flight cases were interrupted and are not counted as completed.
The malformed values are already present in recorded tool arguments; this does not establish whether model generation or provider schema handling caused them.
The replacement starts a new suite signature. No failed scores are relabeled or imported.

finding: The two initialization-blocked attempts called listModels before session creation. The backend then rejected both Gemini IDs as unavailable. Separate fresh-runtime probes accepted the exact IDs and recorded them on replies. Merely switching host configuration did not resolve the discovery-order discrepancy.
resolution: Retain catalog policy checks in a discovery process, then use a fresh isolated inference process for explicit unlisted requests. The temporary user-host option was removed; the replacement matrix retains isolated host and session configuration.
limitations: Initialization failures are not pricing or safeguard failures by either model.
Original raw results remain unchanged locally; no failed scores are imported into the replacement matrix.
The discovery-order behavior was reproduced, but its underlying backend cause is not established.
